offence_severity: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine
number_of_offences: Charged under Section 493 IPC; upheld by trial court, appellate court, and High Court
key_evidence_accepted: There was sufficient documentary evidence to induce a belief to the complainant that she had been lawfully married to the accused although they had not been married according to the rituals. The accused had executed an agreement of marriage and filed an application for registration of their marriage under the Special Marriage Act. In several official documents, she had been shown to be the wife of the accused.
witness_credibility: The witnesses appeared in the Court and supported the relationship of the accused with the complainant as husband and wife. The accused accepted her as his wife in writing in presence of the witnesses.
trial_duration: Dates of offence: not stated; Trial judgment: not stated; High Court decision: 08.09.2005; Supreme Court decision: 24.11.2010
legal_representation: Deba Prasad Mukherjee for the Appellant; D Ratan Kumar Chaudhary for the Respondent
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction; High Court: Upheld conviction; Supreme Court: Appeal placed before Chief Justice of India for referral to another Bench
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused had deceitfully induced the complainant to believe that they were lawfully married, leading to cohabitation and the birth of two children, thereby fulfilling the ingredients of Section 493 of the Indian Penal Code.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the accused did not deceive the complainant into believing they were lawfully married, as there was no formal marriage ceremony or registration, and the complainant was not under the belief of a lawful marriage.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a criminal statute must be construed strictly, and all ingredients of the section must be satisfied for an offence to be established.
precedent_relied_upon: Moideenkutty Haji and others Vs. Kunhikoya and others, AIR 1987 Kerala 184; Dr. A.N. Mukerji Vs. State, AIR 1969 Allahabad 489
